 Photo by: Imagn.com Four Blue Devils Earn NWSL Playoff Bids; Kick Off Action This Weekend
 11/6/2026 1:00:00 PM | Women's Soccer
 Share: DURHAM, N.C. – Four former Duke women's soccer standouts — Tess Boade , Michelle Cooper , Carina Lageyre and Mary Long — are represented on three clubs competing for a National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) championship as the 2026 playoffs begin this weekend.
The four Blue Devils represent three clubs in the eight-team postseason field. Cooper and Long compete for the fourth-seeded Kansas City Current, Lageyre plays for fifth-seeded Angel City FC and Boade represents top-seeded Gotham FC.
Saturday's quarterfinal will feature Blue Devils on both sides as Kansas City hosts Angel City at noon ET at CPKC Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. The match will air live on CBS and Paramount+. Kansas City enters the postseason riding a five-match winning streak.
Cooper, the 2022 MAC Hermann Trophy winner, finished the 2026 regular season with five goals and five assists in 24 appearances, including 22 starts. The forward logged 1,718 minutes and registered 35 shots, including 15 on goal, helping Kansas City secure a home quarterfinal match.
Long has missed the entire 2026 campaign recovering from a knee injury. 
Lageyre is making her first NWSL playoff appearance after signing with Angel City ahead of the 2026 campaign. The midfielder has made an immediate impact during her rookie season with Angel City, appearing in 25 matches with 21 starts. Lageyre totaled two assists across 1,881 minutes while recording 34 tackles and completing 81 percent of her passes.
Boade and Gotham will host eighth-seeded Seattle Reign FC Sunday, Nov. 8 at 12:30 p.m. ET at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey. The quarterfinal will air on ABC. Gotham secured its first NWSL Shield and the postseason's No. 1 seed with a 2-0 victory over Utah in its regular-season finale.
Boade appeared in five regular-season matches between Bay FC and Gotham this season, making two starts and logging 191 minutes. After joining Gotham in August, she started the club's final two regular-season matches, including its Shield-clinching victory over Utah.
The Kansas City–Angel City winner will face the Gotham–Seattle winner in the semifinals, ensuring at least one former Blue Devil advances to that round. The semifinals are scheduled for Nov. 14-15, with the NWSL Championship set for Saturday, Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET at Audi Field in Washington, D.C., on CBS and Paramount+.
